messages.subject: fMRI model regressors
messages.body_plain:
Hi

Thank you for this fantastic and very timely software.

Would you be able to let me know how far into the future extraction of fMRI model regressors might be implemented into the package? I am interested in the IGT, potentially. Is there a workaround in the meantime? Also, is there a way to covary IQ in this task?

Thanks again for excellent work!

Luke.

messages.subject_clean: VPP_delta; something strange about the fitting results
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Woo Young Ahn,

Thank you for your reply! I think it's very helpful. However, I still have some questions.

I also applied the PVL_Decay model and the PVL_Delta model to the IGT behavioral data.

For the PVL_Decay model, the fitting results also showed significant differences between the two subgroups in one parameter.

For the PVL_Delta model, the markov chains did not converge although I tried many kinds of prior distributions.

Do you have any suggestions about this kind of case? By the way, when will the improved model be included in the hBayesDM package? I want to see if it works better than these models I've tried.

在 2017年12月27日星期三 UTC+8下午5:33:50，Pengyu Zhang写道：

> Dear all,
>
> I am using the VPP_delta model in the hBayesDM package to study addiction individuals. However, there is something strange about the fitting results.
>
>
>
> I applied this hierarchical Bayesian model to 59 healthy control subjects’ IGT data. The prior distributions of the parameters are shown below. The reason I change the prior distributions is that the markov chains did not converge if the prior distributions are the same as the original settings in the hBayesDM package. Then I randomly split the control group into two subgroups (29 and 30 subjects) and applied VPP_delta model to them respectively. Although the two subgroups were matched according to gender, age and education level, the fitting results showed significant differences between the two subgroups in alpha and lambda. I split the control group into two subgroups randomly again and the fitting results still showed significant differences between the two subgroups. The problem is, the comparison between healthy individuals and patients could be meaningless or unexplainable if we find differences among control subjects.
>
>
>
> Do you have any idea about this kind of case? Is there something inappropriate about this model that results in this problem?
>
>
>
> The fitting results are shown below. ‘lambda’ represents the fitting result of ‘lambda’ parameter before I split the control group (59 subjects in total). ‘lambda1’ represents the fitting result of ‘lambda’ parameter of one of the two randomly split subgroups and ‘lambda2’ represents the other subgroup. There are also some other parameters that are different in the two subgroups but mainly alpha and lambda. The fitting results are basically the same when I split the control group into two subgroups randomly again.
>
>
>
> Looking forward to your reply. Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: VPP_delta; something strange about the fitting results
messages.subject_clean: VPP_delta; something strange about the fitting results
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Pengyu,

Before answering, I just want to clarify a few points:

1) Do your controls show a large amount of variability in the raw data? If the models are not converging with all 59 subjects, it is possible that there is a lot of variability in response patterns within the control group. This could cause large discrepancies between parameter estimates of each subset.

2) For assessing the difference between parameters of subgroups, what technique are you using? The plot you attached shows what appears to be posterior means of individual subjects, but to compare groups it is important to look at the distribution over the group-level distributions. This can be done with the plotHDI command if you subtract the distributions from each other (e.g., hBayesDM::plotHDI(group1$parVals$mu_lambda - group2$parVals$mu_lambda)). If you are using the means of the posteriors for each subject and not acknowledging the entire posterior (e.g. running a t-test), this will be biased toward showing a difference between groups due to hierarchical shrinkage.

As for the problems with convergence, what are the problems that you are running into? Are the chains mixing too slowly? Are they getting stuck and not moving at all? Are individual chains sampling from different parts of the parameter space (i.e. multi-modal posteriors)? If you attach a traceplot of your results (e.g., plot(fit, type = "trace")), we may be able to offer more specific advice.

I hope this helps!

Best,

Nate

messages.subject: Re: fMRI model regressors
messages.body_plain:
Hi Luke,

For extracting fMRI model regressors—this is something we would like to do soon, but I am unsure on the exact timeline. In the mean-time, you may want to take a look at the .stan code for the go/nogo models (i.e. gng_*.stan). Those models already work, and if you feel comfortable modifying the IGT .stan code to extract the relevant information, it should work just fine.

For covarying values with external data, the package will not do this automatically right now, but it should be something that could be done in the .stan codes with some modification. For example, if the learning rate is assumed to covary with IQ, then you could make each subjects' individual-level learning rate (A) a linear model of some base learning rate (e.g. A0) and the effect of IQ on the learning rate (e.g. A1). Then, each subjects' learning rate would be:

A[i] = A0[i] + A1[i] * IQ[i]

where i indexes the subject number. If the group-level distribution over the effect of IQ (mu_A1) ends up being no different than 0, then the inference would be that IQ does not influence learning rate (at least not assuming a linear relationship). I should note that there are many other ways to do this, but this is the first that came to mind.

Best,

Nate

messages.subject: bandit2arm function for the analysis of Pavlovian learning task
messages.subject_clean: bandit2arm function for the analysis of Pavlovian learning task
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I really appreciate your work and hope that the package will be further developed!
I'm a newbie to computational modelling and so my question is not very technical but more conceptual. But I hope you can still help me to figure it out.
I would like to apply bandit2arm_delta function to a classical rather then instrumental paradigm. In our task in each trial participants see on a screen one of two possible cues(blue or yellow) which is followed by presentation of a reinforcer (either unpleasent or neutral picture). The reinforcement scheme is 80%, by which I mean that for example after a yellow cue they have 80% chance to see an unpleasent picture and 20% chance to see a neutral one. The task is to predict (during cue presentation) what will happen - unpleasent or neutral picture (choice).
I'm confused about interpretation of such choice and outcome. Should the choice still be coded as 1 (unpleasent) and 2 (neutral) while outcome as 1 (for any unpleasent event) and 0 for any other (neutral). Or maybe the outcome 1 should mean the correct guess (result consistent with the expectation) and 0 (or -1?) meaning no consistency between the expectation and result?
>From the literature I know that the Rescorla-Wagner rule is used for clacssical conditioning, but I have trouble to translate it form instrumental learning, where people have a real choice, to Pavlovian learning, where the response does not impact on the outcome.
I actually tried analyzing my data in a way I described above (choice: 1-unpleasent, 2-neutral; outcome: 1-unpleasent, 0 - neutral) but the alpha rate was extremaly close to 0 for all participants, which suggests no learning. Now I'm wondering wheter my interpretation of data was wrong or they actually didn't learn. Also, I'm not sure if I need inverse temperature parameter here.

I'll be happy to with any suggestions!
Thank you,
Emilia
